title: Recognition of the cartesian envelope inside the relative exponential
statement:
Let $\mathcal D$ be an infinity category with finite products, including a terminal object for the empty product. Use the cocartesian and cartesian fibration conventions of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] and symmetric monoidal infinity categories of [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification]. Let $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$ and let $\mathsf{Fin}_*$ be finite pointed sets. Define $\Gamma^\times$ to have objects $(\langle n\rangle,S)$ with $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and one arrow over a pointed map $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ whenever $\alpha^{-1}(T)\subseteq S$. Let $v:N(\Gamma^\times)\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be its cartesian projection. Let $q:Q\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be the relative exponential of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] for $v$ and $\mathcal D$, so that simplices over $\sigma:\Delta^k\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ are coherent diagrams $\Delta^k\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}N(\Gamma^\times)\to\mathcal D$. Write $B_n$ for the reverse-inclusion poset of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let $P\subseteq Q$ be the full simplicial subcategory spanned by the fiber diagrams $f:N(B_n)\to\mathcal D$ such that every restriction cone $f(S)\to f(\{i\})$, $i\in S$, is a product cone, including $f(\varnothing)$ terminal. Then the restriction $p:P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ is a cocartesian fibration, with its cocartesian edges exactly the edges of $P$ that are $q$-cocartesian. Singleton restriction gives equivalences $e_n:P_n\simeq\mathcal D^n$, and these are the Segal equivalences induced by the inert projections; in particular $p$ is a symmetric monoidal infinity category. Cocartesian transport along $\alpha$ is represented by $f\mapsto(T\mapsto f(\alpha^{-1}T))$. For $f\in P_n$, $g\in P_m$, $c_i=f(\{i\})$ and $d_j=g(\{j\})$, restriction induces a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\alpha}_{P}(f,g)\simeq\prod_{j=1}^m\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}\left(\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}c_i,d_j\right).$$
Composition is substitution of the block maps with the projection-preserving regrouping of products, and indices sent to the basepoint are discarded. An edge is $p$-cocartesian exactly when all its block maps are equivalences; for inert $\alpha$, each block is a singleton. Finally the full-subset section $s(\langle n\rangle)=(\langle n\rangle,\{1,\ldots,n\})$ defines, by the relative-exponential evaluation, a coherent functor $\pi:P\to\mathcal D$ with $\pi(f)=f(\{1,\ldots,n\})$. Its inert projections exhibit $\pi(f)$ as the product of its singleton values, its restriction $P_1\to\mathcal D$ is an equivalence, and it sends cocartesian arrows over the active maps $\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ to equivalences. Here active means all non-basepoints map to $1$. Thus $(P,\pi)$ is the specified product-diagram cartesian structure; all the transport, evaluation and composition formulas are restrictions of the simplicial operators of $Q$.

source.place: Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5(1)--(5), the product-diagram subcategory and its identification with the cartesian envelope.

proof.text: Work in a universe containing $\mathcal D$, enlarging the universes in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] if necessary. The indexing categories $\mathsf{Fin}_*$ and $\Gamma^\times$ are small. First, $v$ is a cartesian fibration in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Since $\Gamma^\times$ has at most one arrow over each pointed map, $v$ is faithful, and the map of nerves of ordinary categories is an inner fibration. For $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ and $(\langle m\rangle,T)$, the arrow $(\langle n\rangle,\alpha^{-1}T)\to(\langle m\rangle,T)$ over $\alpha$ is cartesian: given $(\langle k\rangle,R)\to(\langle m\rangle,T)$ over $\alpha\beta$, the inclusion $\beta^{-1}(\alpha^{-1}T)=(\alpha\beta)^{-1}T\subseteq R$ gives the unique factorization over $\beta$, which fills $\Lambda^2_2$; for $\Lambda^n_n$ with $n\geq3$ the horn contains every edge and the missing face commutes because its image in $\mathsf{Fin}_*$ commutes and $v$ is faithful. Apply [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] to this cartesian fibration $v$. This gives the quasicategory $Q$, its cocartesian projection $q$, its stated fibers, and its simplicial operators. More explicitly, for $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$, put $a(T)=f(\alpha^{-1}T)$. The edge from $f$ to $a$ is defined on the indexing category over $[1]$ by $f(S)$ at $(0,S)$ and $f(\alpha^{-1}T)$ at $(1,T)$: an arrow $(0,S)\to(1,T)$ has $\alpha^{-1}T\subseteq S$ and is sent to the corresponding restriction map of $f$. Cartesian indexing edges have $S=\alpha^{-1}T$ and are sent to identities, so the exponential's edge criterion makes this edge cocartesian. For a chain of pointed maps use the same formula with the composite inverse image. Equality of iterated inverse images makes these formulas compatible with every face and degeneracy.

source.place: Notation 2.4.1.2, Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5, printed pp. 284-285: properties of the specified product-diagram model only.

proof.text: Let $A_n\subset B_n$ be the singleton subposet and $j_n$ its inclusion. The order on $B_n$ is reverse inclusion, so $(A_n)_{\geq S}$ is the discrete set of $\{i\}$ with $i\in S$. All its limits exist by finite products, even though $\mathcal D$ is not assumed to have other finite limits. The right-extension and mapping-equivalence clauses of [lem-coef-infinity-finite-poset-kan-extension] give a functor $R_n:\mathcal D^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(N(B_n),\mathcal D)$ with $R_n(c)(S)\simeq\prod_{i\in S}c_i$, counit $j_n^*R_n\simeq\mathrm{id}$, and unit $f\to R_nj_n^*f$. The unit is an equivalence exactly when every restriction cone of $f$ is a product cone, by the pointwise limit formula and the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Hence it restricts to an inverse equivalence for $e_n=j_n^*:P_n\to\mathcal D^n$. At $n=0$ this says that the category of terminal objects is contractible, not that a particular terminal object has been chosen strictly.

source.place: Notation 2.4.1.2, Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5, printed pp. 284-285: properties of the specified product-diagram model only.

proof.text: The transport $a(T)=f(\alpha^{-1}T)$ from step 1 stays in $P_m$ whenever $f\in P_n$. Indeed $\alpha^{-1}T$ is the disjoint union of $\alpha^{-1}\{j\}$ for $j\in T$. For every test object $x$, the product-cone equivalences identify both $\operatorname{Map}(x,a(T))$ and $\prod_{j\in T}\operatorname{Map}(x,a(\{j\}))$ with $\prod_{i\in\alpha^{-1}T}\operatorname{Map}(x,f(\{i\}))$, and the map induced by the restriction cone is precisely this regrouping. This is the defining universal property of the product, including the empty product. For an inner horn in $P$ over a specified simplex of $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$, the inner-fibration property of $q$ gives a filler in $Q$ over that simplex. Its vertices already belong to $P$, so fullness puts this filler in $P$. The explicit horn-cocartesian lifts of step 1 have endpoints in $P$. Applied to the inner fibration $q$, [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] makes their universal mapping squares homotopy pullbacks. The mapping spaces between vertices of a full subcategory are the ambient ones: every simplex in the right-pinched mapping space from $x$ to $y$ has only $x$ and $y$ as vertices, so for $x,y\in P$ it belongs to $P$ by fullness. Thus $\operatorname{Map}_P(x,y)=\operatorname{Map}_Q(x,y)$ degree by degree, and these squares remain homotopy pullbacks when their test objects are restricted to $P$. Applied now to the restricted inner fibration, the converse of the same criterion makes these lifts horn-cocartesian in $P$. Thus $P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ is a cocartesian fibration in the simplicial convention as well as the intrinsic convention of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening].

source.place: Notation 2.4.1.2, Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5, printed pp. 284-285: properties of the specified product-diagram model only.

proof.text:
Fix $f\in P_n$, $g\in P_m$, and $\alpha$, and let $a=\alpha_!f$ be the lift endpoint above. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] the specified horn-cocartesian lift satisfies the mapping square of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Take its homotopy fiber over the identity of $\langle m\rangle$; the lower precomposition map sends this identity to $\alpha$. It gives $\operatorname{Map}^{\alpha}_{P}(f,g)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{P_m}(a,g)$. Since $g\simeq R_mj_m^*g$, the right-adjunction mapping formula of [lem-coef-infinity-finite-poset-kan-extension] identifies the latter space with
$$\prod_{j=1}^m\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(f(\alpha^{-1}\{j\}),g(\{j\}))\simeq\prod_{j=1}^m\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}c_i,d_j),$$
where $c_i=f(\{i\})$, $d_j=g(\{j\})$. Mapping-space invariance under the fiber equivalence is supplied by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. These are the actual maps given by restriction to the cartesian indexing edges, so the natural mapping equivalences compute block components rather than just abstractly equivalent spaces.

source.place: Notation 2.4.1.2, Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5, printed pp. 284-285: properties of the specified product-diagram model only.

proof.text:
Let $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ and $\beta:\langle m\rangle\to\langle\ell\rangle$ be composable, and write their block maps as $u_j:\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}c_i\to d_j$ and $v_k:\prod_{\beta(j)=k}d_j\to e_k$. Restrict the relative-exponential diagram over $[2]$ to the chain of cartesian indexing arrows ending at the final singleton $\{k\}$. The middle value is $g(\beta^{-1}\{k\})$. The natural right-adjunction mapping equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-finite-poset-kan-extension], applied to the transformation $\alpha_!f\to g$, computes its component at this subset from its singleton components: composing with the projection to $d_j$ gives $u_j$ after restriction to $f(\alpha^{-1}\{j\})$. Thus the product universal property identifies that component with the product of the $u_j$, and the long edge has block
$$\prod_{\beta(\alpha(i))=k}c_i\simeq\prod_{\beta(j)=k}\prod_{\alpha(i)=j}c_i\xrightarrow{\prod_j u_j}\prod_{\beta(j)=k}d_j\xrightarrow{v_k}e_k.$$
The regrouping preserves each original factor projection. An index sent to $*$ by either map is absent from every output block. The triangle here is the actual restriction of the diagram defining the simplex in [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential].

source.place: Notation 2.4.1.2, Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5, printed pp. 284-285: properties of the specified product-diagram model only.

proof.text: The higher simplex restriction formulas are definitional. Over a chain $\sigma=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r)$, the indexing category has objects $(t,S)$ and an arrow $(t,S)\to(u,T)$, $t\leq u$, precisely when $(\alpha_u\cdots\alpha_{t+1})^{-1}T\subseteq S$. This follows by taking the ordinary-category pullback along $[r]\to\mathsf{Fin}_*$ and applying its nerve. By the simplicial-operator clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential], restriction along $\theta:[s]\to[r]$ sends a diagram $H$ to the diagram with value $H(\theta(t),S)$ and the same crossing arrow with those endpoints. Its base arrow is $\alpha_{\theta(u)}\cdots\alpha_{\theta(t)+1}$. Deleting an intermediate vertex uses the corresponding triangle of $H$; repeating a vertex inserts an identity. The subsets agree because $(\gamma\beta)^{-1}T=\beta^{-1}(\gamma^{-1}T)$, and these rules commute with iterated restriction because composition of the monotone maps does.

source.place: Notation 2.4.1.2, Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5, printed pp. 284-285: properties of the specified product-diagram model only.

proof.text: For the coherence assertion, invoke [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]: restriction to consecutive edges is a trivial Kan fibration, and its face and degeneracy maps give composition, identities, associativity and all coherent homotopies, naturally in simplicial functors. Apply this to $P$, already a quasicategory by step 3, and to $\mathcal D$ for the indexing diagrams obtained by evaluation. Step 6 identifies their actual simplex restrictions; step 5 computes their composite block maps. The right-Kan unit, counit and mapping-space equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-finite-poset-kan-extension] are natural on precisely the diagrams used here, since their local limits are the finite products verified in step 2. Applying these natural equivalences to the restrictions retains their homotopies as well as their components. Consequently the displayed block substitution and its identities, reassociations and higher compatibilities are those of the given simplices of $P\subseteq Q$.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.8.5, Remark 4.6.8.7, Construction 4.6.8.9 and Propositions 4.6.8.11-12; applied to the actual simplices of HA Construction 2.4.1.4.

proof.text: An edge $f\to g$ over $\alpha$ corresponds by step 4 to a fiber edge $w:a\to g$ after the specified cocartesian lift. The horn-to-mapping-square characterization of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], with the square displayed in [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], says it is cocartesian exactly when precomposition by $w$ induces equivalences of mapping spaces to all fiber test objects; this is equivalent to $w$ being an equivalence. For necessity, the square for the original edge and that for the specified lift, restricted to the target fiber, make precomposition by $w$ an equivalence. Testing at $a$ gives $r:g\to a$ with $rw\simeq\mathrm{id}_a$. Testing at $g$ and using injectivity on homotopy classes gives $wr\simeq\mathrm{id}_g$, since $(wr)w\simeq w=\mathrm{id}_g w$. Thus $w$ is an equivalence. Conversely an equivalence $w$ preserves the lift's universal mapping squares for every test object of $P$, so the original edge is cocartesian. Under $e_m$ and the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], this holds exactly when all block components are equivalences. For inert $\alpha$ each target singleton has exactly one preimage, so these block components are the stated singleton equivalences. For target $\langle0\rangle$ the test is vacuous; for a general empty block it requires an equivalence from the terminal product, as it should. Moreover the corresponding natural transformation $a\to g$ is an equivalence if and only if all its components at subsets are equivalences, by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Applied in $Q$, the edge criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] is exactly this condition. Hence $p$- and $q$-cocartesian edges with endpoints in $P$ coincide.

source.place: Notation 2.4.1.2, Construction 2.4.1.4 and Proposition 2.4.1.5, printed pp. 284-285: properties of the specified product-diagram model only.

proof.text: For an inert projection $\rho_i:\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$, the transport diagram of step 1 has singleton value $f(\{i\})$. Thus the Segal maps are precisely the singleton-restriction equivalences of step 2, after the equivalence $P_1\simeq\mathcal D$. The symmetric monoidal criterion in [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification] applies to the cocartesian fibration from step 3; at $n=0$ it uses $P_0\simeq *$. For evaluation, apply the universal property of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential] to the identity of $Q$ to obtain its evaluation diagram $Q\times_{N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)}N(\Gamma^\times)\to\mathcal D$. Pull it back along the full-subset section to obtain $\pi:P\to\mathcal D$ on all simplices. The section exists since $\alpha^{-1}\{1,\ldots,m\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for every pointed $\alpha$. Under $\pi$, the explicit cocartesian inert projection has map $f(\{1,\ldots,n\})\to f(\{i\})$; these maps form the product cone by the defining condition of $P$. The restriction of $\pi$ to $P_1$ is $e_1$, hence is an equivalence. If $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ is active, its inverse image of $\{1\}$ is the whole source subset, so $\pi$ of the explicit lift is an identity. For every other cocartesian lift, the exponential edge criterion gives an equivalence on this same full-subset cartesian indexing edge; its image under $\pi$ is therefore an equivalence. This includes $n=0$, when both relevant values are terminal. These are exactly the asserted properties of the specified cartesian structure, established entirely in $P$.
